issue.title: Delete by Query failed + Primary/Replica shards out of sync

labels.name: :Distributed/CRUD
labels.description: A catch all label for issues around indexing, updating and getting a doc by id. Not search.

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Elasticsearch 2.3.2

Problem manifests when we run a pretty simple delete-by-query. Here is the response body

```
{
  "took": 1001,
  "timed_out": false,
  "_indices": {
    "_all": {
      "found": 57,
      "deleted": 0,
      "missing": 0,
      "failed": 57
    },
    "index-name": {
      "found": 57,
      "deleted": 0,
      "missing": 0,
      "failed": 57
    }
  },
  "failures": []
}
```

Nothing in the logs indicate a failure. Issuing a _search with the same query yields those 57 document _sometimes_. Ie, the documents are only found on the replica and never the primary. Checking the document delete count on the _cat endpoints yields a 57 document discrepancy too. 

So far, the only solution has been to cancel the allocation of the replicated shared via the _reroute API and let ES rebuild the replica. 

There is a possibility that this is unrelated to delete-by-query directly and it is only surfacing another issue. The general step we take before we realize there a problem is...
1. Switch an alias from pointing to index A to index B
2. Use the reindex API to move documents from A to B
3. Use delete-by-query to purge all moved documents from A

If (1) or (2) have an issue then maybe (3) just surfaces it. 

Some observations: 
- This has happened several times and it's pretty consistent. Probably about 25% of all big move operations
- It's always the replicas that have the extra documents
- We tag the index times on the documents and I never saw clustering on the left-behind documents
- Rebuilding the replica has always worked as a workaround
- When we delete in batch, we have tried both small and large sizes with the same results
- The number of out-of-sync documents is always small (<100)

issue.title: Remove FORCE version_type

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
This was an error-prone version type that allowed overriding previous
version semantics. It could cause primaries and replicas to be out of
sync however, so it has been removed.

Resolves #19769

issue.title: [DOCS] Remove documentation for `force` version-type

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
This option should not be recommended to anyone, and should never be
used, upon chance of primary/replica divergence.

Relates to #19769
